History of Present Illness:
56-year-old man. Two days of upper abdominal pain now localized to the right upper quadrant. Pain is continuous rather than colicky. No jaundice.

Physical Examination:
Right upper-quadrant tenderness and mild localized guarding. Temperature 38.3 C; heart rate 100/min; BP 134/74 mmHg; respiratory rate 20/min; SpO2 98% on room air.

Laboratory Tests:
WBC: 14.0 10^9/L (reference 4.0-11.0)
Hemoglobin: 13.5 g/dL (reference 12.0-17.5)
Platelets: 269 10^9/L (reference 150-400)
Sodium: 137 mmol/L (reference 135-145)
Potassium: 3.9 mmol/L (reference 3.5-5.0)
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL (reference 0.6-1.3)
CRP: 108 mg/L (reference <5)
Lipase: 39 U/L (reference 13-60)
ALT: 62 U/L (reference 7-45)
AST: 50 U/L (reference 10-40)
Alkaline phosphatase: 99 U/L (reference 40-130)
Total bilirubin: 1.0 mg/dL (reference 0.2-1.2)

Imaging Findings:
Ultrasound abdomen: gallstones and distension, but wall visualization is limited. Hepatobiliary scintigraphy: gallbladder remains nonvisualized on delayed images despite bowel tracer activity.
